note: A demo week for an intermediate singer: three practice days of about 30 minutes, built to show many tools in a short week. Leaps are the key skill and return on all three days in new forms: heard in the ear game and sung from Do, heard falling and sung inside a tune, then heard two at once and sung as a harmony line. Around them sit breathwork, the vowel guide, a run past each edge of the range, and from theory a clap-along and a staff-reading block; each day ends with a tune or a line the singer makes up.

plan.title: Week 1: leaps, runs and a line of your own
plan.summary: Three practice days of about 30 minutes. Day 1 is the 4th and the 5th: heard, sung from Do and found inside a tune. Day 2 hears leaps falling, sings five vowels as the note climbs and ends with a run home over chords. Day 3 stretches your range a few notes each way, holds a harmony line over three chords and ends with a line you make up.
plan.progress:
Breath & range: in, hold and out with the count one longer each round; a hiss into a buzz; five vowels as the note climbs to the break; a few notes past each edge of the range. Next: slides across the break.
Intervals & leaps: hears the 4th and the 5th beside their neighbours, and leaps falling; sings the 3rd, the 4th and the 5th up from Do. Next: the octave.
Melodies: a tune that falls a 4th; Do Mi Sol Do as a tune, then a run home over chords. Next: a tune that drops an octave.
Harmony & improvising: hears two notes at once, holds a harmony line over three chords, makes up a line from Do, Mi and Sol over four chords. Next: the harmony line, then one of their own.
Basics: sixteenths tapped on the lane; names the notes on ledger lines. Next: quarters to sixteenths mixed.

days.theme: Falling leaps, vowels and a run home
Your range, a harmony line and your own line
